key_claims.claim: Gravastars can form dynamically from stellar collapse via nucleation and expansion of a de Sitter bubble at the center, without modifying General Relativity
key_claims.evidence_strength: Strong — exact mathematical solution within GR; self-consistent three-region patching; Israel junction conditions satisfied; infinite family of initial conditions leads to gravastar
key_claims.falsifiability: High — predicts specific maximum compactness (C <= 3/8); predicts no event horizon; predicts modified GW ringdown; predicts no Hawking radiation

key_claims.claim: The de Sitter bubble expands like a 'mini-universe' or 'baby universe' driven by dark energy, not unlike the Big Bang
key_claims.evidence_strength: Moderate — mathematically, the de Sitter region is a homogeneous expanding spacetime with Big-Bang-like initial conditions; however, it is bounded by the dust shell and not topologically disconnected; 'mini-universe' is a vivid but defensible metaphor
key_claims.falsifiability: Moderate — requires causal structure analysis; observers inside would experience finite bounded universe, not infinite cosmos

key_claims.claim: There exists a maximum initial compactness C = 3/8 above which collapse to black hole is inevitable
key_claims.evidence_strength: Strong — derived from causal argument (photon must reach surface before dust crosses Schwarzschild radius); robust geometric constraint; only slightly below Buchdahl limit (4/9)
key_claims.falsifiability: High — numerical simulations with different initial conditions can test this bound; any claimed gravastar candidate with C > 3/8 would falsify

key_claims.claim: Gravastars resolve the black hole information paradox because they have no horizon
key_claims.evidence_strength: Moderate — logically consistent: no horizon -> no information loss -> no paradox. BUT: extreme redshift at surface (g_00 -> 0) makes information retrieval practically impossible; and no observational evidence that information is actually preserved
key_claims.falsifiability: Moderate — requires detection of non-thermal radiation from compact object surface; requires distinguishing gravastar GW signatures from black holes

key_claims.claim: JWST 'little red dots' may be dynamical gravastars (Adler 2025)
key_claims.evidence_strength: Weak — speculative interpretation; alternative explanations exist (black hole stars, AGN); no direct structural evidence
